Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

nanodRop 0.2.0

Bug fixes

  • read_nanodrop() no longer strips a trailing “e” from every sample name ending in “e” (e.g. “Rinse” became “Rins”).
  • read_nanodrop() no longer merges measurements that share a sample name.
  • read_nanodrop() no longer returns NA sample names when the instrument writes timestamps in a format other than US 12-hour time. Blocks are now found by their Wavelength (nm) header line.
  • parse_waves() matches wavelengths with a tolerance (tol) instead of exact floating point equality.

Changes

  • read_nanodrop() returns two new columns: measurement (block number in the file) and timestamp.
  • read_nanodrop(): min_wv and max_wv take numbers and default to NULL (keep the full range). Strings such as "190.0" still work.
  • read_nanodrop(): re-measurement handling is now opt-in through remeasure_suffix, and only renames a sample when the original is also present. This changes the default: set remeasure_suffix = "e" to get the old behaviour. The error argument is deprecated.
  • New read_nanodrop_dir() reads every export in a folder.
  • parse_waves() gains type = "ratio" (e.g. A260/A280), tol, and id_cols. By default it now keeps repeated measurements separate. Absorbance columns come before the difference/ratio columns in the output.
  • Removed the magrittr, purrr, readr, rlang, stringr and tidyr dependencies.
  • Corrected documentation for ds and ds1.

nanodRop 0.1.0

  • Initial release with read_nanodrop(), parse_waves() and the example datasets ds and ds1.
